rows.12:7f40:
In the schoolyard, ropes had been strung up around the spot where the high school girl was killed.
There was no body at the spot where the officer had been killed in the video.
"Looks like it hasn't happened yet."
He was certain that a police officer was going to be killed.
And so Tokita waited.
He waited a long time.
But everything around him was hushed and still.
Now and then, a patrol car drove past.
"If I keep hanging around like this, they'll get suspicious of me."
It was just as he was about to head home.{p}
rows.12:8844:
I see.
So you like action?
You can really tell that action movies these days keep getting more and more extreme and intense.
And a lot of them are very well made, too.
But I don't care much for action movies myself.
You see, action movies are nearly always full of stunt people, aren't they?
I can't bear to watch them.
I feel so sorry for them that I can't enjoy the movie.
I find myself wondering whether that stuntman was badly injured afterward, and so on.
I'm timid, you see.
I tend to imagine what goes on behind the scenes for the filmmakers.
That's because in my first year, there was someone in my class who made movies.
Amateur films, mind you.{p}
rows.12:913c:
It showed the hero teaching martial arts forms to the young students of his dojo.
They had shot a scene like that, but this was different from what he remembered.
Tokita was astonished when he watched the film.
Their acting had been so clumsy, yet here they all were, as good as real actors.
Everyone moved swiftly, exactly as he instructed them.
It was almost enough to fool him into thinking his teaching really was that good and they were all improving by leaps and bounds.
That's how well it had been shot.{p}
rows.12:9d98:
"No way...
This is wrong!"
Though if you ask me, it could never have come out that well in the first place, so the whole thing was wrong to begin with.
Tokita thought he might have seen it wrong, and tried to watch it again.{p}Would you watch it again, {a}?
rows.12:9eec:
Then the scene in question came up.
He stared at it, his eyes wide as saucers.
The hero's punch was about to land... or so it seemed.
"Not again★"
The hero's punch only cut through empty air.
The boss's punch slammed into the hero...{p}
rows.12:b2d0:
There, he found a small animal.
It was a creature like a chick, shining silver.
No bird like this exists on Earth.
When you think about that, it should have been eerie, but to Tokita, it looked enchanting.
He decided to keep it in the old school building.{p}
rows.12:c6b0:
How should he edit the footage he'd shot?
He thought it over.
Then he asked the members of the film club for help and decided to turn it into a comic film.
He would raise the problem through laughter. That was his idea.{p}
rows.12:c774:
He started editing.
Editing is a kind of sorcery, isn't it?
With cheerful music, sound effects and the way the film is spliced together, grim footage of bullying turns into a comedy.
Though it also helped that the club members really knew what they were doing.{p}
rows.12:c858:
The comedy was shown at the school festival.
The audience laughed a lot, you know.
Without knowing it was a tragedy that had really happened.
Maybe what's truly frightening is a crowd like that.
As long as they think it's fiction, they can laugh at someone else's misery.
No, even if they knew it was true, they might still laugh.
I even got the feeling they would.{p}
rows.12:f038:
Then one day, Nakayama came down with a cold and was laid up for about four days.
During that time, Tokita did the filming.
He seemed to have some confidence in his own camera skills, too.
Then Nakayama got over his cold, and it seems the shooting wrapped without a hitch.{p}
